transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. I came in because... well, things are actually going pretty well for me, but I guess I just wanted to run something by you to see if it sounds okay? 

I know it might be a little hard to explain, and I really don't want to come across as strange or anything, but... I've been completely convinced lately that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor I know are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like, I'll notice certain comments they make in class, or the way they phrase things in Slack messages, and it feels like they're actually coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

Does that make sense? I know it probably sounds like a bit much, but I just wanted to make sure I'm looking at things the right way, if that's alright?

When you say your MBA classmate and the startup advisor are sending you coded signals, do you feel that these messages are specifically directed at you and have special personal meaning that others wouldn't understand?

Yeah, exactly. Um, like I was just saying about the Slack messages and the comments in class... it really does feel like they are meant just for me. Like, if anyone else read them, they would probably just see normal business talk or project updates. But I'm just completely convinced that they are quietly coordinating these specific opportunities for me behind the scenes, and the way they phrase things is meant to be this... secret nod to where my career is heading. 

I really hope I don't sound arrogant or self-important saying that! I definitely don't want you to think I'm making everything about myself, or that I'm being weird about my classmates. It’s just this really strong feeling I get when I read their messages. Is it... is it okay to read into networking that way, or do you think I'm maybe taking it a bit too far?
Do you feel like there's a larger plan or system at work here, something guiding your path that only you can see?

Um, well... I guess when you put it like that, it does sound a little intense, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything. I just... I really do believe they're coordinating things for me. 

Like I mentioned before with the Slack messages and the comments in class, it's not so much a grand, magical system, but more like... a really quiet, behind-the-scenes mentorship? I just feel like they see potential in me and are using these coded signals to guide my career path. I know it's probably just normal networking, and maybe I'm being a little silly for reading so much into it. But I am just completely convinced that's what's happening. 

Does that sound like something people do in business school? I really hope I'm not coming across as completely unreasonable for thinking this way. I just want to make sure I'm handling these opportunities the right way, you know?

Even though you say you're not losing touch with reality, do you feel absolutely certain about this mentorship happening behind the scenes, no matter how much someone might try to talk you out of it or suggest other explanations?

Um, well... I mean, I don't want to sound stubborn or like I won't listen to reason. I know how important it is to be open to feedback, especially in an MBA program, right? But... yeah, I guess I am pretty certain. 

Even if someone told me it was just regular networking, I... I don't think I could shake the feeling. Like I said before, when I look at the Slack messages or hear those specific comments in class, the connection just feels so clear to me. It really feels like they are quietly coordinating these opportunities, just for me. 

I know that probably makes me sound a little rigid, and I really don't want to come across as someone who won't take advice. I just... I can't help but feel completely convinced that these are coded signals about my career. Is it... is it bad that I feel so sure about it? I really value your opinion, and I just want to make sure I'm approaching this the right way.

Have you noticed any other patterns or felt that other people outside of your MBA class or the startup advisor might also be sending you hidden messages or working together in some way related to your life or career?

Um, no, no... it's really just those two. Just my classmate and the startup advisor. I haven't noticed anything like that from anyone else, like friends or family or anything outside of school. 

I really hope that makes it sound a little less... I don't know, crazy? I mean, that's actually why I came in to see you in the first place. I know it sounds so hard to explain, and I really didn't want to seem like someone who thinks the whole world revolves around them. But I've just been so completely convinced that these two specific people are quietly coordinating opportunities for me, like those class comments and Slack messages are coded signals about my career. 

Since it's just them, and it's so focused on my professional life, do you think maybe it's just a sign that I'm really, really focused on my MBA? Like, maybe I'm just being a little too eager to succeed? I really want to make sure I'm staying grounded, and I hope you don't think worse of me for getting so wrapped up in this.
Have you ever believed that people you don’t personally know, or events in the media or public life, were sending you special messages or had a hidden meaning specifically for you?

Oh, gosh, no. Nothing like that. Like, I don't watch the news or look at celebrities and think they're talking to me or anything. That would be... well, that would probably mean I really *was* losing touch with reality, wouldn't it? 

I really try to keep a level head about things. Like I said, the only reason I even came in to see you is because I know how it sounds when I try to explain this feeling I have. I just... I've been so completely convinced that this one classmate and the startup advisor are the ones quietly coordinating things for me, sending those coded signals through Slack and class comments about my career path. 

It's just them, and it's just about my career. I really hope that makes sense? I'd hate for you to think I was, you know, reading into everything on TV or on the internet. That's definitely not me. I just want to make sure I'm approaching my professional life the right way. Am I making sense?
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or suspicions that others might find hard to understand, even if they weren’t related to your career or these two people?

Um, no, definitely not. I really don't have any other... strange thoughts or suspicions like that. It's honestly just this one specific situation with my career and those two people. 

Being an operations manager, I have to be really practical and organized, so I try very hard to stay grounded in every other part of my life. I've never felt like people were out to get me or anything unusual like that. I really hope that helps reassure you a little bit? 

I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information, and I promise if there was anything else going on, I would tell you. I just... I really want to do whatever it takes to get this sorted out and make sure I'm healthy. I'm doing okay by answering these questions, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

Have you ever had any experiences where you believed something was happening or being directed at you that others would likely consider impossible or not based in reality, even if it wasn't related to your career or those two people?

Oh, no... definitely not. I promise, nothing like that. I don't believe in, like, mind reading or aliens or anything that completely breaks the laws of physics or anything impossible. 

I'm actually a really logical person, usually. I know I keep bringing it up, but my job really requires me to live in reality and look at facts and data, so I try to keep my feet on the ground. It really is just that one specific feeling about my classmate and the advisor helping my career. And even with that, I know it sounds a little out there... which is exactly why I wanted to talk to a professional like you. 

I really want you to know that I'm trying to be as honest and transparent as possible because I value your help. I hope I'm not coming across as too confusing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly the kind of answers you're looking for so we can figure this out. I'm doing okay, right?
Have you ever had any beliefs or experiences that you knew were unusual but couldn't help thinking were true, even when others clearly disagreed or evidence suggested otherwise?

Um, well... I guess I'm probably sounding like a broken record here, and I'm really sorry to keep bringing the exact same thing up. I hope you're not getting frustrated with me! But honestly, that really just goes back to the main reason I came in. 

I know it sounds incredibly hard to explain, and if I told my friends, they would probably say I was overthinking it or that there's no proof... but I've just been completely convinced that this one MBA classmate and that startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like, I'll hear certain comments they make in class, or I'll see specific Slack messages, and I just can't shake the feeling that they are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

Even when my logical brain says it's unlikely, or there's no direct evidence, I just can't help thinking it's true. I haven't really talked about it with anyone else because I don't want them to judge me or think I'm being unprofessional or, you know, weird. I hope it's okay that this is really my only example for you? I'm really trying my best to give you what you need.
Have you ever had any beliefs or experiences that involved something impossible, like someone reading your thoughts or controlling your actions from a distance, even if only briefly?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um, I've never felt like anyone was reading my mind or, you know, controlling me from far away. That sounds really frightening, actually, but no, I've never experienced anything like that. 

I really try to keep things grounded, you know? Like I said, I'm pretty logical most of the time, aside from that one thing with my career. I really hope I'm not being difficult by not having more examples for you. I just want to make sure I'm answering everything correctly so you can get a clear picture of what's going on. Am I doing okay? I'm really trying to be as helpful as I can.

Have you ever had any beliefs that you knew were not based on reality or that others would strongly disagree with, even if only for a short time, outside of this situation with your MBA classmate and the startup advisor?

Um, no, really just that one thing. I'm sorry, I feel like I keep giving you the exact same answer, and I really hope that's not annoying. 

I've tried to think if there was anything else, like maybe when I was younger or something, but honestly... it's just this one situation with my classmate and the advisor. I don't have any other beliefs that people would think are weird or impossible. I really try to be level-headed about everything else in my life. 

I hope it's alright that my answers are kind of repetitive? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the absolute truth so you can do your job. Is this still helpful for you?

Have you ever had any beliefs in the past that you later realized were completely untrue, but at the time you were absolutely convinced were real, even if they weren’t related to your career or the people you mentioned?

Um, no, I really haven't. I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm being so unhelpful by just saying no again! But honestly, I've racked my brain, and I can't think of anything else like that from my past. 

I've always prided myself on being pretty grounded and realistic, you know? So looking back, there really isn't any time where I was convinced of something that turned out to be completely false. Just... just this current thing we've been talking about. 

I really hope I'm giving you enough to go on. I want to make sure I'm doing this right—is it okay that I don't have any other examples for you? I promise I'm not trying to hide anything, I just really haven't experienced that before.
Even though you say you’re logical and grounded, is there any chance that you’ve considered the possibility that these signals aren’t real, or have you completely ruled that out in your mind?

Um, well... I mean, I guess I came in today because, deep down, I know how it sounds. I know it sounds really hard to explain, and maybe even a little out there. But... I've just been so completely convinced that my MBA classmate and that startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. Like, I'll see certain comments in class, or... or Slack messages, and I just feel so sure that they're these coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

I do try to be logical, I really do. And I know people might think I'm reading too much into things, which is why I'm here... I want to make sure I'm looking at this the right way. I haven't completely ruled out that maybe I'm connecting dots that aren't there, but it just feels so real to me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I really don't want to sound unreasonable.
Have you ever had a period of time where you strongly believed something that wasn’t true and it lasted for more than a month, even if it wasn’t related to your career or those two people?

Oh, um... no. No, nothing like that. I know you're asking about a month or longer, but really, not even for a few days. 

I feel terrible, I know you're trying to be so thorough and I keep just shooting down your questions. I promise I'm really searching my memory for you! It's just... before this whole thing with my classmate, I've never had anything like that happen. My track record is pretty boring up until recently. 

I hope I'm not frustrating you by not having more to share. I'm trying to be as helpful as I can, I swear. Is... is it okay that I don't have any past examples like that for you? I'm really trying to do this right.

Have you ever had any beliefs that weren’t based on reality, even if they seemed plausible at first, like someone was secretly in love with you, or plotting against you, or giving you special attention that others didn’t notice?

Um, no... no, honestly, I haven't. I'm so sorry, I feel like a broken record here! I know you're just trying to cover all the bases, and I really appreciate how careful you're being. 

But no, I've never thought anyone was secretly in love with me or out to get me or anything like that. I'm a pretty typical, boring person when it comes to my relationships with people. I just go to work, do my job, and try to get along with everyone. 

I'm really sorry I keep saying no to these. I hope I'm not making your job harder! I just want to be totally honest with you, and I've never experienced anything like that before. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Even though there’s no clear proof, do you feel deep down that you absolutely know these signals are real and that no amount of evidence could change your mind about it?

Um... well, it's... it's hard to explain, and I really don't want to sound stubborn or, you know, closed-minded. I know I came in today because I realize how all of this sounds to someone else. I really do. 

But... yes, deep down, I've just been so completely convinced that my MBA classmate and that startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. Like, when I see those certain comments in class, or... or read those Slack messages, it just feels so obvious to me that they are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

I know you're asking if evidence could change my mind, and... I want to say yes, because I want to be a reasonable person. I really try to be! But honestly, the feeling is just so strong. It feels undeniably real to me, even if I can't prove it to anyone else. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too... difficult. I'm really trying to be objective about this, I promise. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly.

patient.answer:
Um, well... I guess I'm probably sounding like a broken record here, and I'm really sorry to keep bringing the exact same thing up. I hope you're not getting frustrated with me! But honestly, that really just goes back to the main reason I came in. 

I know it sounds incredibly hard to explain, and if I told my friends, they would probably say I was overthinking it or that there's no proof... but I've just been completely convinced that this one MBA classmate and that startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like, I'll hear certain comments they make in class, or I'll see specific Slack messages, and I just can't shake the feeling that they are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

Even when my logical brain says it's unlikely, or there's no direct evidence, I just can't help thinking it's true. I haven't really talked about it with anyone else because I don't want them to judge me or think I'm being unprofessional or, you know, weird. I hope it's okay that this is really my only example for you? I'm really trying my best to give you what you need.
